description_full: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc., an industrial gases company, provides industrial gases, related equipment, and applications to the energy, environmental, and other markets in the Americas, Asia, Europe, the Middle East, India, and internationally. The company produces and sells atmospheric gases, including oxygen, nitrogen, and argon; process gases, such as hydrogen, helium, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and syngas; and specialty gases through on-site gases supply mode or merchant gases supply mode. It also designs, manufactures, and sells equipment for air separation, hydrocarbon recovery and purification, and liquid helium and liquid hydrogen transport and storage; manufactures turboexpanders and other precision rotating equipment; and fabricates helium and hydrogen transport and storage containers. In addition, the company provides cryogenic nitrogen plant, on-site gas generation, cryogenic oxygen plant, PSA hydrogen purification, and membrane separators and systems; and develops, engineers, builds, owns, and operates some of the hydrogen projects, as well as provides air products express services, industrial gas plant services, syngas solutions, and air products smart technology. It serves materials processing, aerospace, analytical labs and research/science, automotive, beverages, bioenergy, biotechnology, cement and lime, chemicals, electronics, food, glass and frit, hydrogen fuelling, industrial decarbonization, lifting, medical, metals production, oil and gas production, oil refining, pharmaceuticals, power, pulp and paper, rubber and plastics, water and wastewater, and welding and cutting industries. Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. was founded in 1940 and is headquartered in Allentown, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc is a large-cap basic materials business with a $71.1B market cap on $13.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years and +3% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 8% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 30%.

The business throws off $477M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 8.80× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
